newsitem.title: USA: Dauphin Tech to acquire electronics contractor.
newsitem.headline: Dauphin Tech to acquire electronics contractor.

text.p: Dauphin Technology Inc, which makes handheld mobile computers, said Tuesday it plans to acquire R.M. Schultz & Associates Inc, an electronics contract manufacturing firm based in McHenry, Ill.
Terms of the stock exchange were not disclosed.
The transaction requires completion by Dauphin of a due diligence review of R.M. Schultz and final closing.

According to terms of a letter of intent, R.M. Schultz will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Dauphin Technology. Richard Schultz, founder and president of R.M. Schultz, will continue to oversee operations its McHenry facility, and report to Dauphin's president and executive committee.

Dauphin said R.M Schultz business will complement its core products and business. The two companies will not depend upon one another for revenue streams or distribution but shared capabilities and synergies can increase business potential, Dauphin said in a statement.
R.M. Schultz has developed electronic musical instruments, and devices used in the medical and computer industries. It has a workforce of 60 employees and its current sales are about $5 million.
Shares of Dauphin were trading off 2/32 to 1-9/32.
